messages:
maya: ok team we are green to start APAC-north1 GPU pool priming. Target window 02:00-05:00 UTC. Goal: soak ~4k tokens/s sustained for 30m, validate autoscaler, verify NVMe warmup and kernel preload. Handoff checklist at end. @sam @tom please confirm probes.

sam: got it. targeting ~4k tokens/s. using synthetic load from loadgen/gpu-worker with batch_size=8, seq_len=1024. ramp plan: 0->60% over 10m, then to 100% over 20m. will push config to the runbook in 2m.

tom: NVMe warmup note: cold starts hit NVMe thundering herd on some nodes. plan is to pre-populate /scratch with model shards via rsync and reduce rsync concurrency. also trigger kernel module preload (nvidia_uvm/nvidia_modeset) before pods pull models.

lia: one-liner to preload kernels (run as root on nodes):
```
for m in nvidia_uvm nvidia_modeset nvidia; do modprobe $m || true; done
```
Also health + cache warm endpoints:
```
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health && curl -sS 'http://localhost:8080/cache/warm?prefix=/models/m1'
```

igor: autoscaler tweaks suggestion: set target_utilization=0.65, scale_up_delay=15s, scale_down_delay=300s, max_pods_per_node=1 (gpu nodes). for mixed-instance pools add buffer_capacity=1 to avoid oscillation.

ops-bot: ramp plan recorded to runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/apac-north1-prime. Will post a progress update every 10m.

deploy-bot: canary deploy completed -> apac-north1/gpu-svc v2.3.1 by maya at 1765043300

maya: starting ramp now (t=0). Observability ask: @sam add per-node nvme_iops, cpu_steal, gpu_util, kv_cache_hits to the dashboard. watch p99 latency and node restarts. if p99 > 250ms we pause.

sam: dashboard added (dash id: infra/prime-1765). initial ramp to 60% QPS in 8m. p99 ~140ms, nvme_iops spike on nodes node-3, node-7, node-12.

tom: seeing network egress flaps on node-7 during parallel rsync (iperf shows burst >1G). reducing rsync concurrency to 4 and re-running prewarm.

maya: nvme prewarm complete on node-7. p99 dropped to 130ms. proceeding to full load.

lia: kv cache prime helper (run inside a worker pod):
```
kubectl exec -n infra $(kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=worker -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -c worker -- /bin/sh -c "python3 /app/scripts/prime_kv.py --prefix /models/m1 --workers 6"
```

igor: autoscaler reacted at t+22m and added 4 nodes; scaling behavior looks stable. suggest tweaking scale_up_delay to 10s for next run if we want faster ramping. no rapid scale-downs observed.

sam: cost FYI: sustained 4k tokens/s here maps to ~1.2 GPU-hours per minute. tagging run with cost-center=eng-infra and setting a soft cap alert at +30% expected.

karen: oncall FYI: enabling extra log retention for +2h. i'll subscribe #incidents and monitor node restarts + p99.

ops-bot: soak run midpoint summary (t+35m): avg tokens/s 3.9k, p99 145ms, autoscaler added 4 nodes, no OOMs detected, nvme prewarm prevented IO stalls on affected nodes. will handoff to oncall in 25m.

maya: handoff checklist for @karen: 1) canary v2.3.1 healthy (yes). 2) NVMe prewarm script committed to infra repo (done). 3) Autoscaler params applied (target_util=0.65, scale_down_delay=300s). 4) Cost tags present. 5) Runbook link posted in channel. If no regressions by t+60m @karen you own it. :thumbsup:

karen: acknowledged. i'll watch p99 and node-restarts. if p99 > 300ms escalate to #eng-sre.

(ops-bot will post final soak artifacts + perf graphs after full 60m window)
